title: fix: answer after tool-only turns when a context engine omits message timestamps
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Sometimes an agent runs a tool and then ends its turn without a final answer. A typical case is a reply of `NO_REPLY` to a `sessions_send` request that needs a result. OpenClaw then runs a short tool-free step to get the answer. That step crashed with `RangeError: Invalid time value` before it made any model call when the session used a context engine that adds messages without a timestamp. Lossless Claw adds summary, focus-brief and recall messages that way. The requester got no answer and the turn was logged as incomplete (incident run `bd2d3478-18a1-4ee0-b7db-43c2d83dd497`, 2026-11-19).

## User Impact

User impact: sessions that use a timestamp-less context engine such as Lossless Claw get a real final answer again after a tool-only turn, instead of an "incomplete turn" error. Ordinary turns send the same model requests as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The tool-free step first trims the turn's messages to fit the model-context limit. To do that it builds temporary bookkeeping entries, and it gave each one a timestamp converted from its message's timestamp. A message without a timestamp made that conversion throw. Every entry now gets the same fixed timestamp. Nothing reads these timestamps: the trimming logic does not look at them, and the entries are never saved or sent to the model. Sizing and model input come from the messages themselves, so request bytes are unchanged.

Rejected alternative: filling in missing timestamps where the context engine's output enters OpenClaw. OpenClaw adds a time stamp to user-message text from the message timestamp, so this would change summary text the model sees. A current time would break the prompt cache, and a fixed time would show the model a 1970 date. A separate Lossless Claw change will add timestamps on the plugin side. This PR is the guard on the OpenClaw side.

Accepted risk: if a later change makes the trimming logic read entry timestamps, this path would give it the 1970 value. The new test checks the trimmed result, not just that nothing throws, so such a change would fail it. No other `new Date(x).toISOString()` call in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner` or `src/agents/harness` converts a timestamp taken from a message. The others use the current clock or validated dates.

## Evidence

**Regression test** (`attempt-history-prepare.test.ts`, two cases). The tool-free step gets a summary-style user message with no timestamp, one with a `NaN` timestamp, and an exec tool call and result. With the default limit, all four messages reach the agent unchanged. With a tight limit, the large tool result is replaced by the usual omission notice while the timestamp-less messages stay. Both cases fail on `origin/main` with `RangeError: Invalid time value` and pass with the fix. Neighboring suites pass: `settled-turn-finalization`, `finalization-scope` and `attempt-prompt-phase` (79 tests). `pnpm check:changed` passes, including typecheck, lint and format.

**Real behavior on the Mac Studio.** Each commit ran in a Crabbox `local-container` lease launched on the Studio (`node:24.22.1-trixie`, image `sha256:f1e03497…`, 8 CPU / 24 GB) from a clone at the pushed commit. Each run used:

- a real isolated Gateway
- the real Claude Opus 5.5 model through ClawRouter, with a pass-through proxy that records request bodies and no headers
- a small test context engine that adds one Lossless Claw-style `{ role: "user", content }` summary message with no timestamp to every assembled context

I used a small test engine instead of Lossless Claw 40833c3 because it isolates the one trigger, missing timestamps, and needs no Lossless Claw database setup. The scenario matches the incident. A requester session asks the model to call `sessions_send` into a WebChat session. There the model runs one `exec`, then replies `NO_REPLY`, which the request does not allow.

| | base `f250a678` (lease `cbx_0c02ea0561f9`) | fix `5f3bb45b` (lease `cbx_b865184e14f8`) |
|---|---|---|
| Tool-free finalization step | crashed before calling the model | ran: one tool-free model request (0 tools, 3,811 bytes; the first message is the timestamp-less summary) |
| Target session's final answer | none (`payloads=0 tools=1`) | a plain-text summary of the exec result |
| What the requester got back | `NO_REPLY_RECEIVED error` | `REPLY: The exec tool ran 'echo settled-proof-01aca19e' once, and it returned 'settled-proof-01aca19e'. …` |
| Side effects | 1 exec | 1 exec (finalization had no tools and repeated nothing) |
| New warnings | 4 failure lines (below) | none; only the expected "running isolated finalization" line |

Base log, which matches the incident. Inside the container the `RangeError` text reads `Invalid Date` because the test runtime uses the OpenClaw Bun fork. Node says `Invalid time value`.

```
[agent/embedded] settled post-tool turn lacked a final answer: runId=a120535b-… — running isolated finalization
[agent/embedded] settled-turn finalization failed: runId=a120535b-… error=Invalid Date — preserving failed recovery
[agent/embedded] incomplete turn detected: runId=a120535b-… stopReason=stop … payloads=0 tools=1 replaySafe=no … — surfacing error to user
[context-engine] discarded unaccepted turn advancement: …: run ended without host acceptance
```

**Ordinary turns are unchanged.** I compared the three model requests whose inputs are the same in both runs: the ordinary turn, the requester's first request, and the target's first incident request. After masking per-run values (container hostname, lease workdir path, UUIDs, timestamps), the request bodies are byte-identical between base and fix, including the system prompt and tools. The raw size difference is 2 bytes in each case, all from the container hostname length.

**CI note:** the first `checks-ui-e2e (1/2)` attempt on `5f3bb45b` ([job 135492776612](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44504325040/job/135492776612)) failed before any test ran. Installing WebKit system packages timed out on the apt mirrors (`WebKit system packages did not download from the fallback archive mirrors (exit 124)`), and `openclaw/ci-gate` failed only because of that job. This was an infrastructure flake, not a failure inherited from main: recent `main` runs of the same workflow are green, and this PR touches only the embedded-runner file and its test. One rerun passed ([job 135515231051](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44504325040/job/135515231051)), and `ci-gate` for that run now passes.

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

On the Studio, from a clone under `~/crabbox-src/sft` checked out at each commit:

```
crabbox run --provider local-container --local-container-image node:24.22.1-trixie \
  --local-container-cpus 8 --local-container-memory 24g \
  --local-container-volume ~/crabbox-proof/sft:/proof --allow-env CLAWROUTER_API_KEY \
  --no-hydrate --timing-json --shell -- 'set -eu; git rev-parse HEAD; \
  corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --store-dir .pnpm-store; \
  cp /proof/settled-finalization-timestamp.proof.live.test.ts src/agents/; \
  SFT_PROOF=1 SFT_PROOF_LABEL=<base|fix> SFT_PROOF_OUT=/proof/out OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 \
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.live.config.ts \
  src/agents/settled-finalization-timestamp.proof.live.test.ts'
```

Both runs exited 0 and both leases reported `"leaseStopped":true`. The proof harness is not committed. The API key was passed only through the environment.

</details>
